children: A recent essay by the comedian Michael Ian Black questioned why so many burly men in pop culture are now going to great lengths to get rid of body hair, remarking that it seems to be "the summer of the hairless he-man." WSJ readers weighed in on the trend with anecdotes, opinions, and of course, a few jokes. Here, edited for length and clarity, are a selection of your comments.
Can you imagine Magnum PI's Tom Selleck or Burt Reynolds absolved of body hair? Inconceivable. -Ronald LaPedis
What do the women think? Literally the only thing that matters. -Christopher Jones

Yeah, um, this has actually been a thing since Tom Selleck parked the Ferrari, Roger Moore stepped down from MI6, and Burt Reynolds ditched his Cannonball Run. Baywatch first aired in Sept. 1989, and David Hasselhoff was the only male actor who still had hair on his chest in that show (which he promptly waxed off later in the series). So the smooth thing has been quite the 'in thing' for men going on 30 years now. Fun fact: Arnold, Stallone and Hulk Hogan all waxed back then too.  -Michael D

I noticed this watching an episode of Reacher. Still, I must object to the sentence phrase, "Now, the ideal man looks like..." I'm not naive enough to argue that men's lives and careers aren't at least partly shaped by their looks, but I argue that "ideal" has a lot less to do with looks than with confidence and wit.  -David Tyler
The smooth look is pure UFC/MMA. Notable exceptions: Sherdog, Ryan Hall, and Shamil "Dadbod" Abdurakhimov.  -Shelley Ashfield
Visual appearance is simply a facade. Manliness is between your ears.  -James Billings

"Retail analysts estimate that the global market for men's grooming (body shaving) will boom by tens of billions of dollars-if not hundreds of billions of dollars-in the next five or so years." And so started the psyops campaign against women's body hair a hundred years ago, for the same profitable reason.  -Mark Jones
My wife absolutely loves the full shag carpeting. As I was typing this, she started laughing and said "hey, make sure you put the word shagadelic" in there........ -John James
Male grooming to me means washing with soap, shaving the face (or trimming a beard) and maintaining a reasonable haircut. Keep the body hair. -Judy Harmon Smith

Armpits are the final frontier. Seems guys will shave anything else but that. Carlos Alcaraz was mostly smooth during the US Open last year (to go with buzz cut) and I think it's a good look with sleeveless shirts. Shaving once or twice a month cuts back on odor significantly (and deodorant works better). Notice how horrified we are when women DON'T shave their pits. Will that day come for men? -Greg Boyer

True story. Our granddaughters (ages 4 and 2) visited last week. Their other grandpa is a cyclist who shaves his legs and arms. I am a cyclist who does not shave my legs or arms. The first night when I went to give the 4 year old a good night hug and kiss, she recoiled and said I was "furry." -Greg Faulkner
